claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
claims.where: spoken (hook, line 1); also post text: title of both looks
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full-text JATS XML of PMC9477388 from ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9477388/fullTextXML; Erdil et al. 2025, PLOS ONE 20(5):e0314612, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314612, article and S2 Table (supplementary .s005) at journals.plos.org; Rosso 2021, Toxicology Reports 8:676-695, doi:10.1016/j.toxrep.2021.03.004, PMC8042289 XML from Europe PMC; images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903 and KSC-as11-40-5877
claims.note: A4: a viewer who swipes at second two leaves believing that Cleopatra's lifetime is nearer to 1969 than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. That is true on every chronology in the cited sources, including the extreme low one, and it does not depend on the exact completion year. Sheisha: Khufu's accession '2613 to 2577 BCE (1σ) according to the 14C-based chronology ... 2589 BCE (2), 2554 BCE (41), or 2480 ± 5 BCE'; Khafre 'ranges from 2586 to 2548 BCE (1σ) ... or 2448 ± 5 BCE'. Even if building ran on to Khafre's accession on Spence's dates (2448), that is about 2,379 years before her birth, against 2,037 years from 69 BC to AD 1969, and from her death in 30 BC it is about 2,418 against 1,998. Sheisha also says materials were brought to the site 'during the reigns of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure'. Menkaure's latest listed accession date (2415 ± 10, Spence) is still about 2,346 years before 69 BC. Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC'; 'The queen committed suicide in August 30 BC'. NASA: 'Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'. The popular form of this fact is the true one. The title card shown with it identifies her as Cleopatra VII (69-30 BC, see n7).

claims.claim: The pyramid was finished around twenty-five sixty BC.
claims.where: spoken (line 2); also post text: description 'completed around 2560 BC'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha 2022 full text (Europe PMC XML) with reference list (33 = Bronk Ramsey et al. 2010 Science; 2 = Shaw, Oxford History of Ancient Egypt 2000; 41 = von Beckerath 1997; 42 = Spence 2000 Nature); Erdil 2025 full text and S2 Table 'The modelled 95% ranges for OK rulers' (journals.plos.org supplementary file pone.0314612.s005)
claims.note: No cited source gives a completion year, as the SOURCES block admits. The figure rests on a premise that no cited source states: that the pyramid was finished before Khufu's reign ended (SOURCES: 'It was finished before Khafre's accession'). Sheisha only names it 'the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu Pyramid)' and mentions 'the construction site of the Great Pyramid of Khufu'. It never says when the pyramid was finished. The SOURCES block also justifies 2560 with 'Erdil 2025 supports it'. Erdil supports the High, radiocarbon chronology ('our results act to reaffirm the High chronological estimates achieved previously'), but its own S2 Table puts the end of Khufu's reign, Djedefra's accession, at medians of 2565, 2577, 2586, 2603 and 2603 BCE across models P1-P5. The 95% ranges are 2602-2528, 2629-2539, 2625-2550, 2638-2561 and 2639-2564, so 2560 falls outside P4 and P5. On the source the script leans on, 'around 2560' is the youngest possible reading rather than the best estimate (A3: the narrower claim the best source supports). Change needed, either (a) or (b). (a) Add an A2 source that the pyramid was complete within Khufu's reign (for example the Merer papyri publication, Tallet 2017, IFAO, 'Les Papyrus de la Mer Rouge I: Journal de Merer', which is in Sheisha's reference list, if it states the date of the casing work, or a standard Egyptological reference with edition). Then rewrite SOURCES entry 1 to record Erdil's S2 Djedefra medians (2565-2603 BCE) and explain why c. 2560 is kept. (b) Move the figure to one the newest chronology centres on, e.g. 'around twenty-six hundred BC' (or 'about 2580 BC'), and update the 'c. 2560 BC' pills, the 2,491 count, 'about 450', the 55.0% scale position and the post description to match. Either way, the premise needs a source.

claims.claim: Two and a half thousand years later.
claims.where: spoken (line 4); also post text: caption 'The Great Pyramid was about 2,500 years old when Cleopatra was born'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha 2022 (Khufu and Khafre accession brackets); Erdil 2025 S2 Table (Djedefra accession medians); Rosso 2021 (69 BC)
claims.note: This is a rounded figure, and it holds across the radiocarbon/High chronology that the script adopts. Completion between Khufu's and Khafre's accessions on Sheisha's 1σ radiocarbon brackets (2613-2548 BCE) gives about 2,479-2,544 years before 69 BC. Completion by Djedefra's accession on Erdil's medians (2565-2603) gives about 2,496-2,534 years. Either way it is 'two and a half thousand'. This rests on the same unstated premise as n2, that the pyramid was complete by the end of Khufu's reign. Once n2's premise has a source, this line needs no change, even under option (b).

claims.claim: From her to Apollo eleven is only two thousand.

claims.source_checked: images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903 ('AS11-40-5903 (20 July 1969) --- Astronaut Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. ... walks on the surface of the moon') and KSC-as11-40-5877 ('Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'); Rosso 2021 (69 BC; August 30 BC)
claims.note: From 69 BC to AD 1969 is 68 + 1,969 = 2,037 years, because there is no year zero. From her death in 30 BC it is 1,998 years. 'Only two thousand' is a fair rounding on either reckoning.

claims.claim: SOURCES entry 6: Menkaure's pyramid 'was begun on an accession date of 2564-2524 BC (radiocarbon) or 2532 BC (Shaw) ... so all three were begun some 2,450 or more years before her birth'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha 2022 XML
claims.note: The quoted dates are right: 'The accession date of Menkaure ranges from 2564 to 2524 BCE (1σ) (33) with centers on 2532 BCE (2), 2489 BCE (41), or 2415 ± 10 BCE (42)'. The inference is not. A pyramid is begun at or after its king's accession, so the accession date is an upper bound on the years before her birth, not a lower one: at most about 2,455 on the late radiocarbon end, and less if work started later. On von Beckerath and Spence it is about 2,420 and 2,346. Change to e.g. 'all three were begun roughly 2,300 to 2,500 years before her birth, depending on the chronology'. The spoken line (n6) is unaffected.
